items.article_search_text: Oscar Piastri believes a 2026 season out of the spotlight could lead him back to the F1 promised land next year. Read more at foxsports.com.au Oscar Piastri’s fourth season has fallen short of lofty standards set by 2025, but the Australian says this year’s struggles come with a silver lining for 2027. Oscar Piastri will look back on 2026 feeling positive about his rate improvement rather than dwelling on his lack of results. Piastri, a championship contender to the final round of last year, has not kicked on in 2026, when sweeping rule changes have thrown him off his game. The Australian has been decisively behind teammate Lando Norris, the reigning champion, for most of the season, even if the margins have been relatively small. Fox Sports, available on Kayo Sports, is the only place to watch every practice, qualifying session and race in the 2026 FIA Formula One World Championship™ LIVE in 4K | Get Kayo now > McLaren’s relative lack of competitiveness for much of the year has been an additional difficulty, though Piastri has been a step behind Norris at the few rounds at which the car has been a genuine victory threat. But McLaren has seen signs of progress from the Australian as the year has progressed, and in Singapore last month CEO Zak Brown said Piastri was fundamentally back to where he was in 2025 in terms of his confidence with the car despite few headline results to show for it. As just one example, despite finishing sixth in Brazil behind the victorious Norris, Piastri’s race pace was respectable for much of the grand prix. Though he admitted 2026 has “definitely been tough”, Piastri told the F1 website that he was finding joy in “trying to make progress”. “I've always tried to remove results from what success looks like,” he said. “Of course results do help, but especially when you're not in a position to win races — whether it be because of the car or the kind of struggles I've had this year — sometimes a win and a successful weekend looks like improvement rather than perfection. “That's brought me joy for sure. There's been some very strong weekends this year that I've been really happy with. [I’m] just trying to work through those things.” The contrast between Piastri and Norris this season has been stark, particularly at the weekends when more has been up for grabs, with the Englishman rarely dropping an opportunity this year. However, it’s been clear from early on that there would be little on the line for McLaren and its drivers this year. Mercedes’s strong start all but guaranteed both titles, even if the field has closed during the year. The team is fourth in the standings and chasing Red Bull Racing for third, while Norris and Piastri are unlikely to finish higher or lower than sixth and seventh respectively in the drivers championship. The team’s step down under new regulations has been a blessing in disguise for Piastri, who has had a chance to do his learning without the pressure of needing to contend for a title in the hope that he’ll be ready for a championship challenge next year if circumstances allow. The same applies to some of the weaknesses that undermined his 2025 campaign later in the year. “Even some of the challenges from last year, they weren't completely dissimilar to what I've got this year, and I feel like I've definitely made a lot of progress on that in general,” he said. “These last few races are definitely going to be another challenge in terms of testing where I'm at, in terms of developing those skills. “Having that challenge has been tough, obviously, but getting through it and then continuing to work on it [is] ultimately going to be rewarding and [will] hopefully set me up for whatever car we get [in future]. “Definitely between myself and the pretty close and intimate engineering team around me, we've learned a lot about each other and how we get the most out of ourselves [as well as] how we get more out of ourselves. "That's been a good process to go through for sure.” Oscar Piastri vs Lando Norris, 2026 so far Qualifying head to head: Norris leads 13-7 Qualifying differential: Norris ahead 1.7 places Time differential: Norris faster by 0.111s (dry only) Race head to head: Norris leads 10-4 Race differential: Norris ahead 1.9 places Race pace differential: Norris faster by 0.3s Points: Norris leads 246-152 (62–38 per cent) Some of the changes to the cars this season have played into Piastri’s weaknesses. The cars are generally lower in grip given the reduced aerodynamic load, and the Australian is at his best when he can exploit high-grip conditions. Further, though, is the way the 2026 car wants to be hustled. Whereas in previous seasons Piastri has been able to achieve a car’s peak performance by driving fractionally below the limit, this year’s car prefers to be pushed to or beyond the limit at all times to deliver its best. Piastri isn’t as comfortable reacting to a peaky car — and the problem has been exacerbated by McLaren’s 2026 challenger being particularly unpredictable at the limit, as even Norris has complained. “You really have to drive the car on the edge all of the time — certainly our car, I don't know what others think of it,” he said. “You're always driving on the edge to an extent, but this year it's really always taking you beyond the edge of trying to salvage things. It's felt quite different to previous [cars] and even a lot of the previous cars I've driven in general. “That's been quite an adaptation process, and learning to trust the car and retrain what feels like the limit is never an easy thing to try and adapt. “It's been tougher than I expected with trying to get to grips with the car … it's definitely thrown in a lot of challenges, and I feel like I've had to change a lot of things in how I drive or certainly tweak things. “But I feel I'm making some progress now in the second half of this year, so [I’m] just trying to continue that.” MORE FORMULA 1 'DID IT FOR AUSTRALIA': How Ricciardo’s ‘bogan’ act came to define his F1 wins... and the ‘loose’ history that inspired it SILLY SEASON: Final piece left in F1's 2027 driver puzzle as Red Bull finally makes contract call 'NOT THE REALITY': Alarming truth about F1's 'new dynasty' claims... and what it means for 2027 Though third in the constructors championship will be of limited consolation to the team that won the last two titles — notwithstanding the boost in prize money — the final three weekends of the season are critical to Piastri and McLaren preparing for a 2027 both hope will bring far bigger prizes. “Everyone is still very determined to get back to where we know we can be,’ Piastri said. “I think we're on our way back there; development and upgrades have always been a strong point for us, and hopefully we can just keep pushing. “The teams around us have definitely raised the bar, but I know that we can raise it even higher.” Oscar Piastri splits from F1 legend manager Mark Webber Motorsport: Liam Lawson will remain with Racing Bulls for the 2027 Formula 1 season alongside teammate Arvid Lindblad after the team confirms its unchanged driver line-up.

It was a "mutual decision [https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/piastri-and-management-team-mutually-terminate-agreement.a59N6pYIBGSiFmwMY1Xkk]" between the two parties, ending their partnership after eight years. Piastri, now 25 years of age, hired Mark as his manager in 2019. Mark, also an Australian, is a former F1 driver who raced for Minardi, Jaguar, Williams, and Red Bull. The partnership made sense back then, especially with Piastri vying for motorsport's most coveted seat. There's still no news about Piastri's search for a new management structure. He is still under contract with McLaren through the end of the 2028 season, so he might not be rushing into this decision. DRIVERS CALL FOR IMPROVEMENT ON THE PIRELLI TYRES Several drivers have criticized Pirelli's wet-weather tyres following the dangerous conditions in the recently concluded Sao Paulo Grand Prix [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/f1-stock-watch-who-gained-and-lost-more-after-the-sao-paulo-grand-prix]. Norris, who won in Interlagos for the second straight year, said that the Pirelli intermediate and full wet tyres could be even more dangerous in Las Vegas, especially if drivers "can't ge any tyre temperature." Along with Norris, the two Red Bull drivers called for improvements on the tyres. Isack Hadjar complained of severe aquaplaning, while Max Verstappen likened the Pirelli tyres to a rock when they're cold. Tyres will play a pivotal role in the upcoming Las Vegas Grand Prix on November 22. The cold desert night could be too much for the tyres, if Pirelli doesn't do anything to improve them. VANDOORNE GETS A JAGUAR SEAT IN FORMULA E Stoffel Vandoorne will join Jaguar TCS Racing for the 2027 Formula E season. The Belgian driver has already won a Formula E championship while driving for Mercedes-EQ in 2022. Vandoorne, 34, was a member of McLaren's Young Driver Programme in 2013. Three years later, he made his Formula 1 debut, replacing Fernando Alonso at the 2016 Bahrain Grand Prix. He finished P10 in his first F1 race. He transitioned to a permanent seat in 2017, before leaving McLaren at the end of 2018. SAO PAULO EXTENDS F1 DEAL THROUGH 2035 We're getting more of these exciting, usually rainy races in Interlagos. items.article_search_text: Oscar Piastri and the structure led by Mark Webber ended their agreement by mutual consent after seven years of relationship. Oscar Piastri has made one of the most important decisions of his sporting career: the Australian McLaren [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/mclaren]driver and the management team led by Mark Webber and his partner, Ann Webber, have agreed to end their professional relationship by mutual consent, according to a joint statement issued this Monday. News that represents a turning point in the young driver's trajectory, who, since 2019, has entrusted his career to the experience and contacts of the former Formula 1 driver. "I would like to thank Mark and Ann for all their support and advice over the years. Their guidance has been invaluable, especially as I navigated the start of my F1 career. I wish them all the best in the future," Piastri declared in the statement. The 25-year-old driver, currently in seventh place in the drivers' championship, faces a new stage under a renewed management structure whose details have not yet been made public. Oscar Piastri: 'Back to Where I Wanted to Be' as McLaren Struggles Ease [https://deweb-519a7.b-cdn.net/post-images/e8b2c1d7-3f6b-41b2-bd82-cc2cf0a73d37.jpeg] Oscar Piastri: 'Back to Where I Wanted to Be' as McLaren Struggles Ease The Australian admits that the start of the season was hard, but assures that the last races have been a turning point. [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/oscar-piastri-back-to-where-i-wanted-to-be-as-mclaren-struggles-ease] Mark Webber, nine-time Grand Prix winner, also wanted to say goodbye with words of gratitude and pride: "We are proud to have played a fundamental role in the formative years of Oscar's career and to have placed him in F1 so that he could compete at the front so early. After our reduced on-track involvement this season, we have collectively agreed that now is the right time to end our management agreement. This will allow Oscar to build on his achievements under a new management structure and us to embark on our new ventures. We wish Oscar all the best for a long and successful career," the Australian noted. Piastri's relationship with the Webbers dates back to 2019, when the young driver won his first single-seater championship with a Formula Renault Eurocup title and secured a place in Renault's Formula 1 junior program. That marked the start of a meteoric rise: the following year he became FIA Formula 3 champion, and in 2021 he repeated the title in Formula 2; his talent was evident, but his arrival in Formula 1 was not without obstacles. Alpine, the renamed Renault team, missed the chance to promote him to a full-time seat, which opened the door for McLaren to sign him. F1 2026: Updated Teammates' Head-to-Head After the Sao Paulo GP [https://deweb-519a7.b-cdn.net/post-images/c80f6a21-5816-430f-a848-568b4309ba77.jpeg] F1 2026: Updated Teammates' Head-to-Head After the Sao Paulo GP Here's a look at the updated teammate head-to-head race records after the 2026 Formula 1 São Paulo Grand Prix. [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/f1-2026-updated-teammates-head-to-head-after-the-sao-paulo-gp] Mark Webber engineered that move: he negotiated with McLaren and secured an agreement for Piastri to debut in Formula 1 in 2023, replacing his compatriot Daniel Ricciardo. The decision proved a success: Piastri scored two podiums in his rookie season and, the following year, took his first Grand Prix win in Hungary. In 2025, already consolidated as one of the most promising drivers on the grid, he starred in an impressive title fight that he finally lost to his teammate, Lando Norris. This year, the Webbers had reduced their presence at the circuits, and Piastri had increasingly relied on other figures in his environment, such as his former race engineer at Prema, Pedro Matos, and his mental coach, Emma Murray. The separation, though friendly, marks a new stage in the Australian driver's career. His future at McLaren seems assured in the short term, but his new management team could open new doors for him in the driver market. Meanwhile, Piastri remains focused on his on-track performance and his objective of fighting for the title again in 2027. His talent is beyond doubt, and his decision to take the reins of his career is another step toward sporting maturity. items.article_search_text: Australian F1 driver Oscar Piastri and former racer Mark Webber have mutually ended their management agreement after nearly seven years. The announcement made on November 9, 2026, after Webber's reduced trackside involvement during the 2026 season. The decision has sparked reactions among fans, with some expressing concern about Piastri's future and others viewing it as a natural career transition. "we are proud to have played a pivotal role in the formative years of oscar's career. we have collectively agreed that now is an appropriate time to bring our management agreement to a close. Oscar Piastri, the Australian McLaren Formula 1 driver, has now parted ways with Mark Webber, the former F1 racer, and his partner Ann after almost seven years of working together.The official announcement on November 9, 2026, marked the end of their professional relationship together.Webber had played an important role in Piastri's journey from junior racing categories to the Formula 1 grid, which included his move to McLaren in 2023 also. Here’s the full story.Several social media platforms shared posts regarding the official statement featuring Mark Webber announcing the end of his management partnership with Oscar Piastri on November 9, 2026.According to the announcement, Webber, along with his partner Ann, will no longer manage the Australian driver after working with him for nearly seven years. Both have confirmed this the day after the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.In the official statement, Mark expressed his pride in the pivotal role played during Oscar's formative years, mainly their contribution of getting him into competitive Formula 1 at an early stage of his career. He also highlighted his reduced trackside involvement during the 2026 season and explained that they have mutually agreed on bringing the management agreement to an end.The announcement said, “We are proud to have played a pivotal role in the formative years of Oscar’s career and to have placed him in F1 so that he could compete at the front so early in. Following our reduced trackside involvement this season, we have collectively agreed that now is an appropriate time to bring our management agreement to a close. This will allow Oscar to build on his achievements under a new management structure and for us to embark on our new ventures.”Oscar Piastri also thanked Mark and Ann Webber in the same joint written statement.He said, “I’d like to thank Mark and Ann for all their support and advice over the years. Their guidance has been invaluable, particularly in navigating the beginning of my F1 career. I wish them all the best going forward.”Mark Webber and Ann had begun managing the F1 driver back in 2019, when he was still competing in junior racing categories.One of their significant contributions came up during Piastri's transition from the Alpine's junior programme to the McLaren just ahead of the 2023 season.After the departure of Fernando Alonso from Alpine, Piastri was among the drivers who were considered for a race seat, but after a contractual dispute, he then eventually secured a McLaren seat.The move was proved to be significant for his career and also allowed him to make his Formula 1 debut with McLaren in 2023.After that, the F1 driver had established himself as one of the team's leading drivers, as he recorded race victories and pole positions.He had also emerged as a championship contender during the 2025 season after spending a period at the top of the standings before he finished as third overall.Ahead of the 2026 season, during the pre-season testing in Bahrain in February 2026,Oscar had brought up additional support for his team, which included Prema Formula 2 race engineer Pedro Matos and mental coach Emma Murray. At that time he described the changes as just a practical arrangement rather than any kind of disagreement between Webber and him. He had also clarified at that time that the relation between Webber and him was on good terms.He said, “There wasn't anything specific; we just made a decision for things to look a bit different. Mark is still very much involved, and I've been in contact with him a lot over the last few weeks. He just won't be trackside as much anymore. So that's really the extent of it. But yeah, there was nothing specific that triggered it.”On a podcast, The High Performance Podcast, titled “The Most Composed Driver in F1: Oscar Piastri Tells His Story", which got released on April 26, 2026, the F1 driver addressed the relationship with Webber, saying it was good after the trackside changes.He said, “The relationship’s good. Very thorough, is Mark. When I first got into F1, Mark was coming up with questions and ideas that literally hadn’t even entered my brain. I would hear him say it and go like, ‘How the hell did he think of that?’ Or like, ‘How am I ever going to think of that?’”“There’s naturally less and less for Mark to do on the racing side of things the more experienced I become. But especially in the first couple of years, there are some lessons you have to learn the hard way, and there’s no other way of doing it, but I’m sure there could have been plenty of other slightly annoying, tougher lessons to learn that I was probably spared because of Mark’s experience and Mark’s guidance.”However, the announcement on November 9 confirms the end of the agreement.As the announcement was made, there were reactions from fans on social media platforms, mainly on X (formerly Twitter).An X user commented that “Webber taught him all he knew about losing a WDC to his teammate. The pupil has outgrown the teacher as of now.”Other X users expressed, “This is not good for Oscar's career; I am genuinely afraid for his future.”“Unfortunately we need him more than ever…”"Did not see that split coming this early,” and “I really need him to hire somebody who will fight for him and for his interest; I really hope he knows what he's doing.”Some said for his comeback, “We need you back.”While fans continue to theorise, the decision seems to come up as a mutual agreement rather than after any disagreement between the two.With the management partnership now officially over, attention will turn to who Piastri chooses to represent him next as he looks to build on his Formula 1 career, with fans hoping the change works in his favour.

items.article_search_text: Oscar Piastri ends his management partnership with Mark Webber, marking a new chapter in the McLaren F1 driver’s career. Oscar Piastri and Mark Webber end their management partnership. Seven years together close. Piastri faces a new career move. Oscar Piastri has ended his management partnership with Mark Webber and Ann Webber, closing a relationship that began in 2019 and spanned his rise from junior racing to Formula One. A joint statement released on the Monday after the São Paulo Grand Prix said both sides had mutually agreed to end their management agreement. The announcement followed a tough, winless weekend for the McLaren driver, who finished sixth in São Paulo. The timing puts a personal change alongside a demanding stretch on track, but the statement offered no suggestion that the decision alters Piastri’s position with the team. For a modern F1 driver, management reaches well beyond race-weekend logistics: it can shape commercial deals, media commitments and longer-term career planning. The agreement’s end is a significant management change, but it concerns representation, not Piastri’s racing contract or his relationship with McLaren. Why Piastri and Webber’s management partnership mattered Webber, a nine-time Grand Prix winner, had guided Piastri since the Australian’s junior-category days. That long view gave the partnership a distinctive role: Webber knew the pressures of the Formula One paddock first-hand, while Piastri climbed through the ranks towards a seat at McLaren. Their collaboration also carried weight because Piastri’s route to F1 involved a high-profile dispute over his future before McLaren confirmed him for 2023. His driver management team helped steer the early stages of a career that has since put him in the fight at the front. Readers can revisit Piastri’s Formula One profile and the earlier contract story in his commitment to McLaren. A change in representation does not, by itself, signal a change in sporting direction. There is no announced replacement in the available statement, and neither side set out a reason for the decision; the confirmed fact is a mutual agreement to end the arrangement. In a sport where every move invites speculation, that distinction matters. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v88_aw4mRkqw What the management change means for Piastri’s next move Piastri now faces the practical task of deciding how to handle the commercial and off-track work previously managed by the Webbers. Whether he appoints a new representative or takes a different approach remains unannounced. For now, the partnership ending marks an administrative reset, not evidence of a wider career move. The immediate sporting focus stays with McLaren. Piastri’s results, qualifying pace and contribution to the team’s championship campaign will define his season far more than a change in driver management. His recent on-track story has included both promise and setbacks, as this report on Piastri’s impact alongside Lando Norris shows. That separation is especially important as teams and drivers plan around Formula One’s changing demands in 2026. A new representative could influence how opportunities are assessed, but it cannot alter the car’s performance or Piastri’s role in the cockpit. The measure of this decision will emerge in the choices that follow, not in assumptions about the agreement itself. Webber’s seven-year involvement ends with mutual thanks rather than a public dispute, according to the joint announcement. For Piastri, the next chapter begins with the same immediate brief: deliver for McLaren on track while deciding who will guide the business of his motorsport career. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v667C2CzSAsM As a sports journalist trained on the trackside and by the pitch, I live to the rhythm of race weekends and match nights. I love numbers and strategies, but above all, the human stories behind performance. At home in the paddocks as much as in amateur clubs, I stand for sports that are accessible to everyone. I write with the rigor of an analyst and the passion of a fan who never misses a session.

Phillip's passion for racing grew even more when his family moved to Europe and he became acquainted with the extraordinary world of Grand Prix racing. He was an early contributor to the monthly French F1i Magazine, often providing a historic or business perspective on Formula 1's affairs.
